title: Barcelona Complete €29 Million Signing of Karim Adeyemi From Borussia Dortmund
excerpt: The 24-year-old German winger reunites with coach Hansi Flick in Catalonia, becoming Barcelona's second major summer signing as the club reshapes its attack after Robert Lewandowski's departure.
body:
• Barcelona agreed a €22 million fixed fee plus €7 million in performance-related add-ons for the 24-year-old German international, with Dortmund retaining a 20% sell-on clause.
  • Adeyemi signed a five-year contract until 2031, reuniting with coach Hansi Flick, who gave him his senior Germany debut in 2021.
  • The deal follows Anthony Gordon's £70 million arrival from Newcastle and fills attacking gaps left by Robert Lewandowski's move to Chicago Fire and Marcus Rashford's return to Manchester United.
  • Barcelona remains in active pursuit of Atlético Madrid's Julián Álvarez as Flick continues an aggressive squad overhaul for the new season.

FC Barcelona on Wednesday confirmed the signing of German winger Karim Adeyemi from Borussia Dortmund, adding another attacking weapon to Hansi Flick's rapidly evolving squad. The LaLiga champions announced that Adeyemi has signed a contract through June 2031.

"FC Barcelona and Borussia Dortmund have reached an agreement for the transfer of forward Karim Adeyemi, who has signed a contract with the Catalans until 2031," the club said in an official statement.

Deal Structure and Finances

The transfer is worth an initial €22 million, with a further €7 million in performance-related bonuses tied to appearances and titles, according to multiple reports from SPORT and other Spanish outlets. Dortmund also secured a 20% sell-on clause in any future transfer, a common safeguard for clubs parting with young talent. Adeyemi will earn approximately €6 million net per season at Camp Nou.

Club president Joan Laporta, who had delayed the formal announcement while attending Spain's triumphant FIFA World Cup campaign in the United States, confirmed the presentation upon his return to Barcelona on Tuesday. "He will be presented tomorrow," Laporta told reporters at El Prat Airport.

A Reunion With Flick

The move carries a personal dimension for Adeyemi, who reunites with Flick after the coach handed him his senior Germany debut during his two-year spell as national team manager. According to reports, Adeyemi told his agent Jorge Mendes as early as May that Barcelona was the only club he wanted to play for, calling the transfer a childhood dream.

"Karim Adeyemi suits Hansi Flick's style of play. He is a very good player who can play both on the wings and through the center with both feet. He adds another dimension to the team."

— Gaizka Mendieta, former Spain international

Adeyemi joined Dortmund in 2022 from Red Bull Salzburg and made 146 appearances across four seasons, scoring 36 goals in all competitions. Last term, he contributed 10 goals and six assists in 39 matches. The German international is also renowned for his electric pace — he set a Bundesliga speed record of 36.65 km/h during Dortmund's 5-1 win over Freiburg in the 2022-23 season, according to Reuters.

Reshaping Barcelona's Attack

Adeyemi is Barcelona's second major attacking addition this summer after the £70 million signing of England forward Anthony Gordon from Newcastle United. The spending spree comes amid a significant reshaping of the forward line. Robert Lewandowski departed for MLS side Chicago Fire, Marcus Rashford returned to Manchester United after his loan spell, and Ansu Fati also left the club.

The versatile 24-year-old can operate on either flank or through the center, giving Flick the kind of tactical flexibility his high-pressing system demands. Former Spain midfielder Gaizka Mendieta noted that Barcelona struggled on the wings last season whenever Raphinha was unavailable — a problem Adeyemi's directness and speed should help address.

More Business Ahead

Barcelona's summer window is far from over. The club remains in active pursuit of Atlético Madrid forward Julián Álvarez, though reports suggest Barcelona will wait for the player to push for an exit before making a formal move. Other business includes the potential loan of goalkeeper Marc-André ter Stegen to Ajax and the departures of Roony Bardghji and Marc Casado.

With eight Barcelona players having featured in Spain's World Cup-winning squad, including breakout star Lamine Yamal, the club enters the new season with renewed confidence. Adeyemi could feature as early as this week's pre-season friendly against Europa before Barcelona travels to England for their training camp.

Barcelona's total summer spending has now surpassed €100 million, a clear signal that Flick and the board are committed to building a squad capable of defending the LaLiga title and mounting a serious Champions League challenge.
